source_citation: Gucker, Corey L. (2004), Vachellia constricta, whitethorn acacia, USDA Forest Service Fire Effects Information System. DOI:10.2737/feis-species-review-vaccon

morphology_source_reported.growth_habit: Drought- and cold-tolerant deciduous shrub, to 6 m
morphology_source_reported.stems: Straight, paired nodal spines, 3–6 mm long
morphology_source_reported.leaves: Compound, usually 2.5–5 cm long; FEIS says 3–6 leaflet pairs, exact leaf unit/pinna definition should be clarified from identification flora
morphology_source_reported.nectaries: Extrafloral nectar glands on leaf rachises
morphology_source_reported.roots: Resprouts from root crown following topkill

habitat_source_reported: Arid slopes, mesas, canyons, seasonally wet washes, floodplains and drainages; often sandy/loamy soils with caliche
flowering_source_reported: Typically Apr–Jun; possible second flowering Jul–Oct depending on conditions
cautions: FEIS explicitly states its description was not written as an identification key
1999 Flora does not include a dedicated treatment for Acacia/Vachellia constricta
State-level native status is not evidence for Hays County target range
